docs.title: lazar
docs.text:
The smallest self-evolving agent harness.

One tool: bash(command) — bash, sandboxed. One protocol: skills as filesystem entries. Everything else is emergent.

~/lazar/
├── bin/lazar              the immutable kernel (chflags uchg after build)
├── src/                   kernel source (read-only after build)
├── scripts/               kernel ceremony helpers + lazar-chat.sh wrapper
├── skills/                the agent's "being" — capabilities as folders
├── memory/                durable notes
├── workspace/             scratchpad, the agent's cwd, projects you build
└── logs/stream.jsonl      append-only event stream (kernel auto-rotates at ~10MB)

docs.title: Tent-pole features
docs.text:
1. The agent can't lie about what it did — VERIFY contract When the agent claims it created, rotated, or fixed a file, the kernel parses its [VERIFY] block and re-checks every claim against the real filesystem (stat, exists, contains) before accepting the answer. Failed claims force a correction turn; a second failure ends the run with grounding_failed. "Done" is verified, not trusted — and the check is compiled into the kernel, so the agent can never patch it away.

2. Sealed kernel, evolving agent — Architecture The runner is locked with chflags uchg after build. The agent can read its own source but can never modify it. All growth happens in skills/ — markdown files the agent reads and writes itself. New capability needed? The agent authors a new skill. The kernel stays small and permanent; the being grows.

3. Every event, on disk, forever — Sessions & memory The kernel appends everything — prompts, responses, tool calls, results, verify reports — to an append-only JSONL stream, and deliberately does not auto-load it into the next conversation. Memory management, context loading, summarization, recency heuristics: all of it lives in skills, where it can evolve. Nothing is hidden in a black-box database.

4. One tool, full power, real guardrails The agent gets exactly one tool: bash(command), run through sandbox-exec. Write zones, blocked paths, and command vetoes are enforced at the syscall boundary — not by asking the model nicely. Guardrails can be toggled off explicitly (lazar-guardrails.sh off), and the system prompt tells the agent which mode it's in so it never guesses.

5. Delegation with receipts — Sub-agents bin/lazar-spawn runs child agents for isolated, file-verifiable work. Child prompts must be stranger-complete (absolute paths, a SUCCESS line, EXPECT-VERIFY claims authored by the parent), and the spawn binary re-checks the child's declared claims before reporting success. Bounded retries, wedged-child kills, recursion depth caps — no runaway agent trees.

6. A lifecycle you can hook — Hooks protocol User-controlled scripts in hooks/<event>.d/ fire at session-start, user-prompt, pre-tool, post-tool, session-end, and tick. Hooks can inject context, veto tool calls, and shape behavior — without touching the kernel.

docs.title: What is lazar?
docs.text:
lazar is a small Rust runner that gives a language model exactly one tool — sandboxed bash — and gets out of the way. There is no autopilot, no planner framework, no plugin SDK. State lives on disk. Everything else is emergent.

The kernel does three things:

  1. Takes a prompt via -p.
  2. Calls an Anthropic-protocol model endpoint (SSE-streamed) with one tool, bash(command).
  3. Runs the bash through sandbox-exec and feeds the output back.

docs.title: The bet
docs.text: A language model plus one honest tool, a sealed runner, and a filesystem it can grow into is enough. Capabilities are data, not code paths. Trust is enforced, not assumed. The interesting parts — memory, judgment, delegation, self-repair — are all skills, which means they improve every session instead of waiting for a kernel release.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Every LAZAR_* variable below was enumerated by grepping src/ and bin/lazar (grep -rhoE 'LAZAR_[A-Z_]+' src bin | sort -u) — this list is ground truth from the binary, not from memory. Provider keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, MINIMAX_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) come from the same sweep plus memory/PINNED.md.

docs.title: Provider / auth
docs.text: Variable Purpose ANTHROPIC_API_KEY API key sent as x-api-key / Authorization: Bearer to the provider endpoint. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Override the API endpoint (e.g. https://api.minimax.io/anthropic, https://openrouter.ai/api). MINIMAX_API_KEY MiniMax key, stored in ~/lazar/.env; the launcher maps it into the request auth. LAZAR_ENV_OWNED_API_KEY / LAZAR_ENV_OWNED_AUTH_TOKEN / LAZAR_ENV_OWNED_BASE_URL Mark which credential vars the kernel itself set (so it doesn't leak or double-override them in children). LAZAR_KC_SERVICE / LAZAR_KEY_NAMES Keychain service name and the list of key names the kernel knows how to fetch.

docs.title: Model / request
docs.text: Variable Purpose LAZAR_MODEL Model id for the invocation (overrides the built-in default). LAZAR_MAX_TOKENS Response cap per API call (default 8192 — exceeding it in one write is the classic big-write truncation abort). LAZAR_MAX_TURNS / LAZAR_MAX_TOOL_CALLS Hard ceilings on agent-loop turns and tool calls per invocation. LAZAR_STALL_NUDGES Bounded stall-recovery nudges per invocation (default 2). Fires only when the final sentence narrates unfinished intent; never on questions, never unbounded. LAZAR_GROUNDING_RETRIES How many correction turns the kernel allows after a failed [VERIFY] contract before returning grounding_failed.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text: Variable Purpose LAZAR_HOME The harness root (default ~/lazar). Everything keys off this. LAZAR_BIN / LAZAR_LOGS / LAZAR_MEMORY / LAZAR_SKILLS / LAZAR_WORKSPACE Per-directory overrides for bin/, logs/, memory/, skills/, workspace/. LAZAR_INHERITED_CWD / LAZAR_INHERITED_ADD_DIRS Cwd and extra allowed directories passed down to a spawned child.

docs.title: Logging / sessions
docs.text: Variable Purpose LAZAR_LOG_MAX_BYTES Rotation threshold for logs/stream.jsonl (default ~10MB). LAZAR_LOG_ARCHIVE_KEEP How many rotated archives to keep. LAZAR_SESSION_ID Current session id; set by the kernel, consumed by hooks and the TUI. LAZAR_SESSION_HISTORY_MAX_BYTES Cap on how much prior-session history is prepended on --resume. LAZAR_ENV_QUIET Suppress non-essential env/banner output.

docs.title: Tools / sandbox
docs.text: Variable Purpose LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX 1 disables the sandbox-exec profile for the invocation (full operator filesystem access). LAZAR_GUARDRAILS Guardrails mode (on/off); toggled by the guardrails skill via scripts/lazar-guardrails.sh. LAZAR_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS Wall-clock timeout per bash tool call. LAZAR_TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES Cap on captured tool output returned to the model. LAZAR_TOOL_ENV Extra KEY=VAL entries injected into tool environments. LAZAR_TOOL_INHERIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY 1 lets a spawned child inherit the parent's API key. Default is isolation — children spawned without this fail auth with 401 invalid x-api-key. LAZAR_BASH_FALLBACK Allow bash fallback behavior when the primary tool path is unavailable.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Variable Purpose LAZAR_HOOK_EVENT Name of the lifecycle event being fired (session-start, user-prompt, pre-tool, post-tool, session-end, log-rotation, agent-stop, tick). LAZAR_HOOK_PAYLOAD_LEN Byte length of the JSON payload handed to the hook. LAZAR_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECS Per-hook wall-clock timeout. LAZAR_STRICT_PRE_TOOL_HOOKS Strict mode for pre-tool hooks (a failing/vetoing hook blocks the tool call).

docs.title: Sub-agents
docs.text:
Variable Purpose LAZAR_DEPTH Recursion depth of the current invocation (cap is the kernel's MAX_DEPTH, 5). LAZAR_SPAWN_BUDGET Max spawns per session (default 10). LAZAR_SPAWN_CEILING Max retries per task (default 2). LAZAR_SPAWN_TIMEOUT Wall-clock kill for a wedged child (default 300s). LAZAR_SUBAGENT_STATE State dir for spawn bookkeeping (logs/subagent/). LAZAR_SPAWN_TEST / LAZAR_TEST_FLAG_* Test hooks used by skills/_meta/subagent/selftest.sh and kernel tests.

Note

If a variable isn't in this table, it isn't read by the kernel. Verify with grep -r 'VAR_NAME' ~/lazar/src before documenting a new one.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text: --output-format controls what lazar writes to stdout during a run. Three modes, from bin/lazar --help and src/src/main.rs.

docs.title: text (default)
docs.text:
Human-readable: assistant text streams to stdout as it arrives; tool calls are silent. This is the normal interactive mode.

lazar -p "hello"

docs.title: json
docs.text:
One JSON result object emitted at the end of the run — no live output. For scripts that want the final answer as data.

lazar --output-format json -p "2+2?" > result.json

docs.title: stream-json
docs.text:
JSONL events — one JSON object per line on stdout as they happen. This is the machine interface: TUIs, log analyzers, and dashboards consume it.

lazar --output-format stream-json -p "list your skills" | jq -r .type

docs.title: Event types
docs.text:
The same events are also appended to logs/stream.jsonl (with kind instead of type). Observed kinds in src/:

Event Fires when invoke_start Start of an invocation; carries depth and model user The prompt, as received assistant Each assistant message (content blocks) tool_result Result of a bash tool call auto_nudge Kernel stall-recovery nudge fired (bounded by LAZAR_STALL_NUDGES) invoke_end End of invocation; carries stop_reason hook_start / hook_end A lifecycle hook fired; hook_end carries action, exit_code, duration_ms, timed_out tick_start / tick_end A --tick heartbeat run session_continuation Prior session turns were prepended (--session / --resume) sandbox_disabled The kernel printed its no-sandbox warning banner access_policy The resolved access policy for the invocation

docs.title: Sample event
docs.text:
{"type":"invoke_start","depth":0,"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","ts_ms":1714555000000}

{"type":"hook_end","event":"pre-tool","script":"01-deny.sh","action":"veto",
 "exit_code":0,"duration_ms":12,"timed_out":false,"ts_ms":1714555000123}

Consumers should treat unknown type values as forward-compatible noise and keep reading — the kernel may add event kinds without notice.

docs.title: --input-format
docs.text: text (default) takes the prompt from -p. stream-json is reserved: stdin JSONL input is currently treated as text.

docs.title: Provider protocol
docs.text:
There is no lazar-side HTTP server. The "API" surface of lazar is:

  1. The CLI — bin/lazar and bin/lazar-spawn.
  2. The structured --output-format stream-json event stream.
  3. The underlying provider's HTTP endpoint, which the kernel speaks to directly — and which power users can hit with curl just the same.

This page documents (3).

docs.title: The protocol: Anthropic Messages
docs.text:
The kernel is an Anthropic-protocol client. It makes SSE-streamed POST requests to <base>/v1/messages using reqwest, with:

  • x-api-key: <key> — the API key header
  • anthropic-version — the standard Messages API version header
  • one tool declared: bash(command)

Power users can talk to the same endpoint directly — nothing about lazar's side of the wire is proprietary.

docs.title: Endpoint resolution
docs.text:
From src/src/main.rs:

Condition Base URL Default model ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set <your value> (kernel appends /v1/messages) claude-sonnet-4-6 Only MINIMAX_API_KEY set (MiniMax fallback) https://api.minimax.io/anthropic MiniMax-M3 Otherwise https://api.anthropic.com claude-sonnet-4-6

Key resolution: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY first, then MINIMAX_API_KEY. If neither is set the kernel aborts before any network call.

docs.title: Known-good endpoints (from memory/PINNED.md)
docs.text:
• MiniMax (default for this install): native Anthropic protocol at https://api.minimax.io/anthropic — no proxy. Default model MiniMax-M3. Key under MINIMAX_API_KEY in ~/lazar/.env (mode 600).
  • OpenRouter: exposes an Anthropic-protocol endpoint at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/messages that the kernel speaks with no proxy. Routed by the launcher when LAZAR_BACKEND=openrouter (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api).
  • Kimi / Moonshot: https://api.moonshot.ai/anthropic via the LAZAR_BACKEND=kimi launcher preset.

LAZAR_BACKEND is a launcher-level preset selector (used by workspace/lazar-env.sh and lazartui.sh); the kernel itself only reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / MINIMAX_API_KEY, and LAZAR_MODEL. See Configuration.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: The MiniMax /v1/messages endpoint accepts image_url blocks, so the agent can see images (see skills/vision/). OpenRouter's Anthropic-compat endpoint passes image blocks through unchanged.

docs.title: Listing models (MiniMax)
docs.text: GET https://api.minimax.io/v1/models returns the MiniMax model list. The TUI's model picker reads ~/lazar/workspace/tui/models.txt (plus a small built-in fallback) as its source of truth.

docs.title: Secret isolation
docs.text: Tool subprocesses do not inherit ANTHROPIC_API_KEY by default — nested lazar -p calls from inside agent bash fail without a key unless you opt in with LAZAR_TOOL_INHERIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=1. When the sandbox is off, a set of PASSTHROUGH_VARS (SSH agent, GitHub/GitLab tokens, cloud credentials, etc. — see Environment variables) is forwarded so operator CLIs keep working.

docs.title: lazar-spawn CLI reference
docs.text:
bin/lazar-spawn is the only sanctioned sub-agent spawn surface — a locked bash wrapper (installed by setup.sh, chmod 555) that sits between the agent and raw lazar -p recursion. A pre-tool hook vetoes raw lazar -p calls from the agent when the spawn-discipline hook is enabled.

Ground truth below comes from bin/lazar-spawn itself (it's readable bash) and skills/_meta/subagent/SKILL.md.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
lazar-spawn [--lint-only] [--detach] <task-id> <prompt-file>
lazar-spawn --status|--await <job-id>
Flag Effect --lint-only Validate the prompt file against the lint rules and exit — no child spawned --detach Spawn in the background; returns a job id immediately. Finalize later with --status / --await --status <job-id> Print the current job JSON envelope --await <job-id> Poll until the job finishes or LAZAR_SPAWN_TIMEOUT expires

docs.title: Prompt file requirements
docs.text:
The child is context-blind — a stranger with a filesystem. The prompt file must be self-contained:

  • at least one absolute path
  • a SUCCESS: line
  • an EXPECT-VERIFY: block with indented claims: exists=/abs, contains=/abs:needle, size_at_least=/abs:bytes

The recommended pattern is a context pack: pack-and-spawn.sh writes a BRIEF.md under workspace/tasks/<id>/ (objective, absolute I/O paths, SUCCESS/EXPECT-VERIFY claims, relevant skills, constraints, out-of-scope, and a RESULT.md protocol), then dispatches a thin prompt pointing at the BRIEF.

bash "$LAZAR_HOME/skills/_meta/subagent/pack-and-spawn.sh" <task-id> \
  --objective "..." --out /absolute/deliverable

docs.title: Gate on claims
docs.text:
The wrapper re-checks EXPECT-VERIFY claims against the filesystem after the child exits — the child's self-report is not trusted. The stdout envelope is JSON:

{"status":"ok","job_id":"...","task":"...","matched":true,"output":"/path/to/out.log"}

On failure you get {"status":"fail","matched":false,"failed_claims":[...]} listing exactly which claims did not hold. Trust matched, not child prose. On matched:false, fix the BRIEF and retry within the ceilings below.

A sweeper handles wedged jobs: if a detached worker's pid dies before finalizing, --status/--await re-runs the stored claim check from the child's out-log and finalizes the job itself.

docs.title: Bounds
docs.text:
1. Kernel stall-nudges (in-child recovery, bounded)
  2. Per-task ceiling LAZAR_SPAWN_CEILING (default 2)
  3. Session budget LAZAR_SPAWN_BUDGET (default 10)
  4. Wall-clock LAZAR_SPAWN_TIMEOUT (default 300s)
  5. Kernel recursion depth cap (MAX_DEPTH = 5)

Budget/job state lives under workspace/subagent/ — see the known tradeoff about why it isn't in logs/.

docs.title: Self-test
docs.text:
bash "$LAZAR_HOME/skills/_meta/subagent/selftest.sh"

See also: Sub-agents integration guide.

docs.title: lazar CLI reference
docs.text:
The complete flag surface of bin/lazar, as reported by bin/lazar --help and confirmed in src/src/main.rs (clap Args struct). Nothing here is invented.

The smallest self-evolving agent.

Usage: lazar [OPTIONS]

docs.title: -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
docs.text:
Prompt for the agent. This is the normal entry point:

lazar -p "build a skill that prints the current time, then use it"

Conflicts with --reset-all.

docs.title: --reset-all
docs.text:
Wipe skills/, hooks/, memory/, workspace/, logs/, and saved access approvals, then re-seed from the kernel (seed skills and hooks are embedded in the binary via include_dir!). Asks for confirmation unless --yes is also passed. The kernel binary itself is untouched. After reset, the agent is at the exact state of a fresh install.

Safety checks in src/src/main.rs refuse to reset an empty, relative, non-canonical, or symlinked LAZAR_HOME.

docs.title: --yes
docs.text: Skip confirmation for --reset-all (destructive, non-interactive).

docs.title: --verbose
docs.text: Verbose mode: prints tool calls, depth, and stop_reason to stderr.

docs.title: --model <MODEL>
docs.text: Override the model. Falls back to $LAZAR_MODEL, then to the built-in default claude-sonnet-4-6 (or MiniMax-M3 when running in MiniMax-fallback mode — see Configuration).

docs.title: --output-format <FORMAT>
docs.text:
Output format. Default: text.

Value Behavior text Human-readable: streams assistant text to stdout; tool calls silent json One JSON result object emitted at end (no live output) stream-json JSONL events — one JSON object per line on stdout as they happen (for TUIs, log analyzers)

See Output formats for event shapes.

docs.title: --input-format <FORMAT>
docs.text:
Input format. Default: text.

Value Behavior text Prompt comes from -p as a plain string (default) stream-json Reserved: prompt comes as JSONL events on stdin. Currently treated as text

docs.title: --tick
docs.text: Heartbeat: fire all hooks under hooks/tick.d/ and exit. No model call. Wire this to launchd / cron for scheduled work (memory consolidation, summary enrichment, etc.). Conflicts with -p and --reset-all. See Hooks.

docs.title: --session <SESSION>
docs.text: Session id for multi-turn conversation continuity. When set, prior turns from logs/sessions/<id>.jsonl are prepended to the message array, and new events are appended to that log. The same flag both creates the log on first turn and continues it on subsequent turns. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 - _ . (max 64 chars, no path traversal). Conflicts with --resume.

docs.title: --resume
docs.text: Resume the most recently modified session log automatically — equivalent to --session <newest>. Useful for referential prompts ("ok do that", "yes", "fine") when you don't remember the session id.

docs.title: --no-sandbox
docs.text:
Disable sandbox-exec for this invocation. The agent's bash runs with full operator privileges instead of the restricted sandbox profile. Use when working outside ~/lazar (e.g. running lazar from a project directory and having it edit project files). Also enabled via LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX=1.

Security

With the sandbox disabled, the agent can read, write, and execute anywhere the operator can — including ~/.ssh, dotfiles, and system paths. The kernel emits a loud banner on every invocation when active.

docs.title: --cwd <PATH>
docs.text: Set the working directory used by every model-issued bash command. The path must already exist and is canonicalized before any hook or tool runs.

docs.title: --add-dir <PATH>
docs.text: Add an existing directory to the sandbox's write allowlist for this invocation. Repeat the flag to approve multiple project roots.

docs.title: -h, --help
docs.text: Print help (summary with -h, full with --help).

docs.title: Exit behavior
docs.text:
• Depth guard: invocations nested deeper than MAX_DEPTH (5) abort with recursion depth <n> exceeds max 5.
  • Budget guards: the loop aborts with aborted after reaching LAZAR_MAX_TURNS=… or LAZAR_MAX_TOOL_CALLS=… when the caps are hit.
  • Grounding: a terminal response whose [VERIFY] claims fail twice ends in a non-zero grounding_failed result.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Normal invocation
lazar -p "what skills do you have?"

# Multi-turn session
lazar --session refactor -p "step 1: inventory the project"
lazar --session refactor -p "ok, do step 2"     # prior turns are visible

# Scoped project access
lazar --cwd ~/code/proj --add-dir ~/code/proj -p "inspect this project"

# Structured output for a TUI
lazar --output-format stream-json -p "hello" | jq -r .kind

# Heartbeat (no model call)
lazar --tick

docs.title: Helper scripts
docs.text:
One-line descriptions of the scripts in ~/lazar/scripts/, taken from each script's own header comments. These are operator tools — they run in your terminal, not inside the agent loop.

Script Purpose kernel-build.sh Rebuild the kernel and relock. Run after editing src/. If the build fails, the source stays writable so you can fix and retry. Pass LAZAR_GUARDRAILS=off to keep the kernel writable across rebuilds. kernel-edit.sh One-shot: unlock, open main.rs in $EDITOR, rebuild, relock. For quick kernel edits. kernel-verify.sh Run patch-specific verification for a kernel proposal — looks for workspace/proposals/<name>/verify.sh and executes it (exports LAZAR_PROPOSAL_DIR / LAZAR_PROPOSAL_NAME). kernel-apply.sh Apply a staged kernel proposal from workspace/proposals/<name>/: diffs against the current kernel, prompts for confirmation, then backs up, applies with delete semantics, rebuilds, and re-locks. kernel-unlock.sh Unlock the lazar kernel source/binary for editing. Pair with kernel-build.sh. lazar-guardrails.sh One switch for ALL enforcement layers: off (full operator access — no sandbox, unlocked kernel), on (restore enforcement), status (which mode am I in?). lazar-chat.sh Minimal interactive REPL for lazar. No dependencies beyond bash; pipes assistant text through glow for markdown rendering when available. lazar-spawn.sh The trusted sub-agent spawn surface — installed to $LAZAR_HOME/bin/lazar-spawn by setup.sh (chmod 555). The copy in scripts/ is the source; agents call the locked binary. new-proposal.sh new-proposal.sh <name> — copy the proposal skeleton to a new proposal dir under workspace/proposals/. migrate-from-clawd.sh Move an older install at ~/clawd/lazar to the new default home ~/lazar. Preserves skills/, memory/, workspace/, logs/; supports --yes for non-interactive migration.

Related reading: Kernel guardrails for the proposal ceremony and Sandbox for the guardrails switch.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
lazar is a small immutable kernel plus a large writable everything-else. The split is the whole design.

~/lazar/
├── bin/lazar              the immutable kernel (chflags uchg after build)
├── src/                   kernel source (read-only after build)
├── scripts/               kernel ceremony helpers + lazar-chat.sh wrapper
├── skills/                the agent's "being" — capabilities as folders
├── memory/                durable notes
├── workspace/             scratchpad, the agent's cwd, projects you build
└── logs/stream.jsonl      append-only event stream (kernel auto-rotates at ~10MB)

docs.title: The kernel
docs.text:
The kernel is a single Rust binary (bin/lazar, source in src/). It is a runner, not an autopilot. It:

  1. Parses CLI args (clap) — see the CLI reference.
  2. Assembles a system prompt from src/system-prompt.txt plus runtime identity (active model, API endpoint) and hook-injected context.
  3. Runs an agent loop against an Anthropic-protocol /v1/messages endpoint, exposing exactly one tool: bash(command).
  4. Executes each tool call through sandbox-exec with the profile compiled in from src/sandbox.sb (unless --no-sandbox / LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX=1).
  5. Appends every event (prompts, tool calls, results, hook fires) to logs/stream.jsonl, auto-rotating at LAZAR_LOG_MAX_BYTES (default 10 MB).
  6. Fires lifecycle hooks at deterministic moments (session-start, user-prompt, pre-tool, post-tool, session-end, log-rotation, agent-stop, tick).
  7. Enforces VERIFY grounding: when the agent ends a turn claiming file outcomes, the kernel parses its [VERIFY] block and re-checks every claim against the real filesystem. Failed claims trigger a bounded correction turn (LAZAR_GROUNDING_RETRIES, default 2), then a non-zero grounding_failed result.

Bounded limits keep runaways in check: LAZAR_MAX_TURNS (50), LAZAR_MAX_TOOL_CALLS (200), LAZAR_MAX_TOKENS (16384), LAZAR_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS (120), LAZAR_STALL_NUDGES (2), and a recursion depth cap of 5 (MAX_DEPTH).

docs.title: The immutable kernel story
docs.text:
After setup.sh:

  • bin/lazar has chflags uchg — OS-level immutable. Not even root can modify or delete it without chflags nouchg first.
  • src/ is chmod -R a-w — the source is sealed.
  • The sandbox profile blocks writes to bin/ and src/ from any agent-run bash command.

The agent can cat its own binary and source — it can study itself — but it cannot modify the runner. Kernel changes go through the proposal ceremony, which requires operator review in an interactive terminal.

docs.title: Seed skills and hooks
docs.text: The seed skills (src/seed-skills/) and seed hooks (src/seed-hooks/) are compiled into the binary with include_dir!. On first run — and after lazar --reset-all — they are extracted to skills/ and hooks/. This makes --reset-all work fully offline: a factory-fresh agent needs nothing but the binary.

docs.title: Where evolution happens
docs.text:
Layer Writable by agent? Purpose bin/, src/ No (locked + sandboxed) The runner skills/ Yes Capabilities — markdown SKILL.md folders memory/ Yes Durable notes, journals, harness lessons workspace/ Yes Scratchpad, projects, task packs, proposals logs/ Read-only (kernel-owned) The canonical event stream hooks/ Operator-controlled Lifecycle scripts

The kernel is capability-blind: dropping a new folder into skills/ makes the capability available immediately — no recompile, no registration. See Skills.

docs.title: Sub-agents
docs.text: Delegation goes through bin/lazar-spawn, a locked bash wrapper installed by setup.sh that lints prompts, bounds retries, wall-clock-kills wedged children, and re-checks the child's declared claims against the filesystem before reporting success. See Sub-agents.

docs.title: Kernel guardrails
docs.text: The Rust kernel is the protected core. Runtime automation, hooks, skills, and model-issued bash may read it, but they must not write to src/ or bin/. There is no Rust-side autopilot or self-evolver that patches or rebuilds the kernel on its own — that is by design.

docs.title: Why the agent can't self-patch the kernel
docs.text:
Three independent mechanisms overlap:

  1. OS locks. bin/lazar carries chflags uchg (OS-level immutable) and src/ is chmod -R a-w after setup.
  2. Sandbox profile. src/sandbox.sb grants writes only to skills/, memory/, workspace/, /tmp, and a few agent-CLI session dirs. bin/ and src/ are not in the allowlist.
  3. Prompt-level doctrine. The system prompt instructs the agent that kernel changes are proposal-only: stage, never apply.

Even with enforcement layers off (see Sandbox — guardrails switch), the proposal flow below remains the supported path.

docs.title: The proposal ceremony
docs.text:
Kernel changes follow a four-step, operator-reviewed flow:

  1. Stage. Write a full proposed source tree under workspace/proposals/<name>/src/. The new-proposal.sh script copies a skeleton; the _meta/propose-kernel-patch skill guides the agent.
  2. Review. scripts/kernel-apply.sh <name> produces a diff against the current kernel for the operator to read.
  3. Confirm from an interactive operator terminal — the script prompts before touching anything.
  4. Apply + rebuild. The script backs up the current source, applies with delete semantics, rebuilds, and re-locks the installed binary. scripts/kernel-verify.sh <name> runs an optional per-proposal verify.sh (via LAZAR_PROPOSAL_DIR / LAZAR_PROPOSAL_NAME).

docs.title: The scripts/kernel-*.sh family
docs.text:
Script Purpose kernel-unlock.sh Unseal the kernel source/binary for editing (pairs with kernel-build.sh) kernel-edit.sh One-shot: unlock, open main.rs in $EDITOR, rebuild, relock kernel-build.sh Rebuild the kernel and relock; on failure the source stays writable so you can fix and retry. Pass LAZAR_GUARDRAILS=off to keep the kernel writable across rebuilds kernel-apply.sh Diff, confirm, and apply a staged proposal from workspace/proposals/<name>/, then rebuild kernel-verify.sh Run patch-specific verification (verify.sh) for a staged proposal

The agent's role stops at step 1. Applying is always an operator act.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: Every bash command the model issues runs through macOS sandbox-exec with a profile compiled into the kernel from src/sandbox.sb — unless the sandbox is explicitly off.

docs.title: What's allowed when the sandbox is ON (default)
docs.text:
• Reads: open. The profile allows file-read* everywhere — the agent can study its own kernel source and binary.
  • Writes: restricted to the agent's writable zones:
    • $LAZAR_HOME/skills/
    • $LAZAR_HOME/memory/
    • $LAZAR_HOME/workspace/
    • /tmp (/private/tmp, /private/var/tmp, /private/var/folders)
    • Specific session/auth subdirs under ~/.codex and ~/.claude (sessions/, todos/, auth.json, etc.) so sub-agent CLIs can update their own state.
  • Network: open, for API calls and skills like web search.
  • Explicitly NOT writable: bin/, src/, logs/ (trusted kernel-owned state), and operator CLI config files like ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/hooks/, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — a sandboxed agent writing those could inject code into the operator's own unsandboxed CLI sessions.

A disallowed write fails with Operation not permitted. The agent is expected to learn from the failure and route around it via a skill — or ask for guardrails to be toggled.

docs.title: The escape hatches
docs.text:
Mechanism Effect --no-sandbox CLI flag Disables sandbox-exec for this invocation LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX=1 env var Same; propagated to nested tool subprocesses --cwd <PATH> Sets the working directory for every model-issued bash command (path must already exist; canonicalized before hooks/tools run) --add-dir <PATH> Adds an existing directory to the sandbox write allowlist; repeatable for multiple project roots

With the sandbox off, the kernel prints a loud banner on every invocation and the agent's bash runs with full operator privileges — it can read/write anywhere the operator can, including ~/.ssh. Only enable when you trust the agent and the model.

Scoped project access example:

lazar --cwd ~/Documents/GitHub/my-project \
  --add-dir ~/Documents/GitHub/my-project \
  -p "inspect this project"

docs.title: The guardrails switch
docs.text:
Enforcement is a switch, not a wall. One script moves all five layers:

scripts/lazar-guardrails.sh status   # which mode am I in?
scripts/lazar-guardrails.sh off      # full operator access
scripts/lazar-guardrails.sh on       # restore enforcement
# Layer Mechanism 1 bash sandbox sandbox-exec (LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX) 2 kernel binary lock chflags uchg bin/lazar 3 source lock chmod a-w src/ 4 pre-tool vetoes hooks/pre-tool.d/*.sh (renamed .disabled, not deleted) 5 agent instructions src/system-prompt.txt + access.rs prompt context

Layer 5 is the one people miss: with layers 1–4 off, the agent can still self-censor if its prompt says a path is forbidden. The current mode is therefore injected into every session by hooks/session-start.d/03-guardrails-mode.sh, and the guardrails skill lets the agent check and flip the switch itself.

State lives in workspace/.guardrails. An explicit LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX always wins.

Known tradeoff

Sub-agent state (bin/lazar-spawn budget counters) lives under workspace/subagent/, which is agent-writable — so an agent can reset its own LAZAR_SPAWN_BUDGET counter. This was a deliberate swap: the state previously lived in logs/ (not agent-writable), which made spawn fail 100% of the time under the sandbox. A working spawn with a soft budget beats a hard budget on a broken spawn.

docs.title: The VERIFY Contract — Kernel-Enforced Honesty
docs.text:
lazar's most distinctive feature: the agent cannot lie about file state, because the kernel — not the model — does the checking.

Most agent harnesses trust the model when it says "done." lazar doesn't. When the agent ends a turn claiming outcomes ("I created the file", "the build passes"), the kernel re-checks every claim against the real filesystem before accepting the response. This page describes how the system works, why it lives in the kernel, and why it matters.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
The system was born from a real failure: an earlier session fabricated a complete report — "I rotated the log, here is the table of new sizes" — without running any tools at all. The operator only caught it by manually running ls -la. Language models are fluent; fluency is not evidence.

The fix could not be a prompt instruction ("please don't fabricate") — the model can ignore instructions, and a self-evolving agent could even edit them away. So enforcement was placed in the one place the agent cannot reach: the immutable Rust kernel.

docs.title: The two enforcement layers
docs.text: Both layers live in src/src/verifier.rs (~1,400 lines, compiled into the lazar binary) and run on every terminal response.

docs.title: Layer 1 — the [VERIFY] block
docs.text:
When the agent claims outcomes, it must end its turn with a machine- checkable block:

[VERIFY]
exists=/Users/jkneen/lazar/docs/mkdocs.yml
size_at_least=/Users/jkneen/lazar/docs/site/index.html:1000
contains=/Users/jkneen/lazar/docs/RESULT.md:DONE
[/VERIFY]

The kernel parses the block (parse_verify_blocks_strict) and re-runs each claim itself (verify_all) with real filesystem operations — stat, existence checks, substring scans (bounded to 8 MB reads). Supported claims:

Claim Meaning exists=<path> file/dir exists not_exists=<path> file/dir absent size=<path>:<bytes> exact size size_at_least=<path>:<n> size ≥ n size_at_most=<path>:<n> size ≤ n contains=<path>:<substr> file contains substring (max 160 chars) mtime_within=<path>:<sec> modified within the last n seconds

Rules enforced by the kernel, not by politeness:

  • Max 8 claims per block — excess lines are rejected as invalid (models that dump 14 fragile contains= claims thrash the correction loop; the cap forces exists=/size_at_least= discipline).
  • Unknown claim keys fail the block even if other claims pass.
  • The closing marker must be exactly [/VERIFY] on its own line.

docs.title: Layer 2 — the pattern detector
docs.text: Independent of the VERIFY block, scan() + should_flag() look for fabrication tells in the response text: past-tense completion language ("I fixed…", "Total time: …"), markdown state tables, and checkmark claims that are not backed by tool calls in the invocation. This layer fires even with no VERIFY block present — one passing claim must not globally suppress unsupported completion language elsewhere in the text.

docs.title: What happens on failure
docs.text:
When claims fail or unsupported completion language is detected:

  1. The kernel rejects the terminal response and injects one bounded correction turn, telling the agent which claims failed. The agent must inspect and repair the real state (or retract the claim).
  2. If the corrected response still fails, the invocation ends with a non-zero grounding_failed result — visible to callers, wrappers, and CI.
  3. The retry budget is LAZAR_GROUNDING_RETRIES (default 2). It is bounded on purpose: grounding failures are loud, never silent.

Every verify report is also logged to logs/stream.jsonl as a verify_report event, so the audit trail survives the session.

docs.title: Why the kernel, and not a skill?
docs.text:
Concern Where it lives Why Claim parsing & filesystem re-checks src/src/verifier.rs (kernel) The agent can read but never modify bin/ or src/ — it cannot patch away its own lie detector Claim formats & when-to-claim guidance system prompt + verify skill Behavioral guidance the agent can evolve — but only toward writing claims that survive the Rust checks Subagent claim gating bin/lazar-spawn (locked binary) Child tasks declare EXPECT-VERIFY claims authored by the parent; the spawn binary re-checks them before reporting success

The split is deliberate: enforcement is kernel-anchored, guidance is evolvable. A self-evolving agent gets smarter about satisfying the contract; it never gets the option of removing it.

docs.title: What this buys you
docs.text:
• Trustworthy "done." When a lazar agent says a file exists with certain content, the kernel has already statted it.
  • Honest failure modes. Agents that hit a wall say so — the alternative (a confident fabrication) is mechanically rejected.
  • Auditable sessions. verify_report events in the event stream give you a post-hoc record of every claim and its outcome.
  • Composability. CI pipelines and wrappers can treat a zero exit code as "the reported state was verified," not just "the model finished talking."

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Architecture — where the verifier sits in the kernel flow
  • Environment variables — LAZAR_GROUNDING_RETRIES
  • Subagents — EXPECT-VERIFY gating for child tasks
  • Skills — the verify skill: the agent-side discipline

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: lazar keeps configuration deliberately thin: a handful of environment variables, an optional .env file, and the model choice.

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
The kernel reads two key variables, in this order:

  1. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — the primary key, sent as the x-api-key header.
  2. MINIMAX_API_KEY — fallback. When only this is set, the kernel automatically targets https://api.minimax.io/anthropic and defaults the model to MiniMax-M3.

If neither is set, the kernel aborts with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set (nor MINIMAX_API_KEY).

Keys live in ~/lazar/.env (mode 600), sourceable by the launcher, or in the macOS Keychain via the env-vars skill (service name lazar, overridable via LAZAR_KC_SERVICE). Never commit secrets.

docs.title: Endpoint and backend selection
docs.text:
• ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL — override the API base. The kernel appends /v1/messages to whatever you set. Default: https://api.anthropic.com (or the MiniMax URL when in MiniMax-fallback mode).
  • LAZAR_BACKEND — not read by the kernel. It is a launcher-level preset selector used by workspace/lazar-env.sh and lazartui.sh to set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL / key / model for you. Known presets include minimax (default), kimi, openrouter, anthropic, and proxy.

The launcher contract mirrors Claude Code:

Claude Code lazar kernel ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN mapped to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (sent as x-api-key) ANTHROPIC_MODEL mapped to LAZAR_MODEL

Usage:

LAZAR_BACKEND=minimax    source ~/lazar/workspace/lazar-env.sh
LAZAR_BACKEND=openrouter source ~/lazar/workspace/lazar-env.sh
LAZAR_BACKEND=kimi       source ~/lazar/workspace/lazar-env.sh

docs.title: Model selection
docs.text:
Precedence (first wins):

  1. --model <MODEL> CLI flag
  2. LAZAR_MODEL environment variable
  3. Built-in default: claude-sonnet-4-6 (MiniMax-M3 when running in MiniMax-fallback mode)

docs.title: Runtime root
docs.text: LAZAR_HOME overrides the install/runtime root (default ~/lazar). All skills, memory, workspace, logs, and hooks resolve relative to it.

docs.title: Tuning knobs
docs.text:
Every operational limit is an env var — see the full environment variable reference. The most commonly tuned:

Variable Default Purpose LAZAR_MAX_TURNS 50 Max agent loop turns per invocation LAZAR_MAX_TOOL_CALLS 200 Max tool calls per invocation LAZAR_MAX_TOKENS 16384 Model output cap per turn LAZAR_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS 120 Wall-clock timeout per bash tool call LAZAR_NO_SANDBOX unset Set to 1 to disable sandbox-exec

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• macOS — the kernel relies on sandbox-exec for the bash sandbox and chflags uchg for the kernel binary lock.
  • Rust toolchain (cargo + rustc) — the kernel is a Rust binary built from src/.
  • An API key for an Anthropic-protocol provider (see Configuration).

docs.title: From a git clone
docs.text:
git clone <repo-url> ~/lazar
cd ~/lazar
bash setup.sh

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
lazar -p "what skills do you have?"

setup.sh builds the kernel with an external Cargo target directory ($LAZAR_HOME/workspace/.cargo-target by default), installs the binary at ~/lazar/bin/lazar, locks it with chflags uchg, and seeds skills/ and hooks/ from the copies embedded in the binary. Re-running setup preserves existing skills, memory, workspace, logs, and source unless you explicitly opt in (LAZAR_UPDATE_SOURCE=1 to refresh source, LAZAR_RESET_ALL=1 for a factory reset after rebuild).

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
~/lazar/bin/lazar --help      # enumerate the CLI surface
~/lazar/bin/lazar -p "hello"  # first end-to-end model call

docs.title: Upgrading the kernel
docs.text:
bash ~/lazar/scripts/kernel-unlock.sh   # unseal src/ + bin/
# edit src/, then rebuild + relock:
bash ~/lazar/scripts/kernel-build.sh

docs.title: Migrating from an older ~/clawd/lazar install
docs.text:
bash ~/clawd/lazar/scripts/migrate-from-clawd.sh

This moves the directory to ~/lazar, optionally updates the /usr/local/bin/lazar symlink, and shows diffs before patching shell rc files (with backups). Use --yes for non-interactive migration. Skills, memory, workspace, and logs are preserved; rebuild the kernel after the move.

docs.title: Factory reset
docs.text:
lazar --reset-all          # asks for confirmation
lazar --reset-all --yes    # non-interactive (destructive)

Wipes skills/, hooks/, memory/, workspace/, logs/, and saved access approvals, then re-seeds the embedded skills and hooks. The kernel itself does not change.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hooks are user-controlled lifecycle scripts. The kernel fires them at deterministic moments; you drop executable bash scripts into ~/lazar/hooks/<event>.d/ and they run in lex order.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event Fires when Veto? Transform? session-start top of lazar -p ..., before first model call (depth 0 only) — inject context user-prompt when a top-level prompt is received — inject context pre-tool before each bash execute() call (every depth) yes rewrite command post-tool after each bash execute() call returns — rewrite output session-end when a top-level invocation ends (success OR error, via Drop) — — log-rotation after the kernel auto-rotates stream.jsonl — — agent-stop when the model emits stop_reason: end_turn (depth 0) — — tick when invoked as lazar --tick (heartbeat path) — —

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
hooks/
├── README.md
├── session-start.d/
├── user-prompt.d/
├── pre-tool.d/
├── post-tool.d/
├── session-end.d/
├── log-rotation.d/
├── agent-stop.d/
└── tick.d/

Scripts must be executable (chmod +x). Files ending in .disabled are skipped. Prefix with a number for ordering (01-, 99-).

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
Each hook receives a JSON payload on stdin:

{
  "event": "pre-tool",
  "ts_ms": 1714555000000,
  "lazar_home": "/Users/you/lazar",
  "depth": 0
}

and may emit one JSON action on stdout (default: continue):

Action Where Effect {"action":"continue"} anywhere do nothing {"action":"veto","reason":"..."} pre-tool block the call; reason returned to model {"action":"transform","command":"..."} pre-tool rewrite the bash command before exec {"action":"transform","output":"..."} post-tool rewrite captured output before posting to model {"action":"inject","context":"..."} session-start / user-prompt append to system prompt as RUNTIME CONTEXT

Multiple transforms in one .d/: last wins (lex order). Any veto on pre-tool blocks the call.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Hooks receive LAZAR_HOME, LAZAR_SKILLS, LAZAR_MEMORY, LAZAR_WORKSPACE, LAZAR_LOGS, LAZAR_HOOK_EVENT, LAZAR_HOOK_PAYLOAD_LEN, plus HOME set to LAZAR_HOME. Per-hook timeout: LAZAR_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECS.

docs.title: Examples shipped with the kernel
docs.text:
• pre-tool.d/00-example-deny-rm-rf.sh.disabled — veto destructive commands
  • session-end.d/00-example-distill.sh.disabled — distill the session
  • log-rotation.d/00-example-summarize-archive.sh.disabled — summarize on rotation
  • tick.d/00-example-daily-distill.sh.disabled — heartbeat distill

Remove .disabled and chmod +x to enable. The spawn-discipline pre-tool hook (the thing that vetoes raw lazar -p) is a real installed example of this mechanism.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: Memory is lazar's persistence layer: plain markdown under ~/lazar/memory/, readable by you and the operator with a bare cat. No JSON blobs, no databases.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Layer Path Purpose Pinned context memory/PINNED.md Read every session start: provider truth, code ownership, anti-stall rules, search rules. Working notes memory/*.md Timestamped notes, breadcrumbs for future invocations. Work journal memory/work-journal.md Durable record of what was built (harvested by _meta/log-harvest). Harness lessons memory/harness/ Ranked durable lessons, managed by _meta/harness/harness.py. Event stream logs/stream.jsonl Canonical append-only log (see Sessions) — recorded, not auto-loaded.

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
# Load at the start of a task
cat $LAZAR_HOME/memory/PINNED.md
cat $LAZAR_HOME/memory/*.md 2>/dev/null

# Append a timestamped note
printf '\n## %s\n\nThe thing worth remembering.\n' \
  "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> $LAZAR_HOME/memory/notes.md

docs.title: The continual harness
docs.text:
Durable lessons go in the harness, not only freeform markdown:

python3 ~/lazar/skills/_meta/harness/harness.py add \
  --kind memory --title "my-lesson-slug" \
  --content "specific lesson" --evidence "what happened"

A compact ranked overview is injected at session-start by a hook. Load full entries with harness.py load <id>; mark usefulness with helpful / unhelpful.

docs.title: Discipline rules
docs.text:
• Recall is always a command, never a promise: cat memory/PINNED.md, bounded tail of the log, rg <topic> memory/work-journal.md.
  • Search works: a ~/lazar/.ignore file makes bare rg see workspace/ memory/ skills/ logs/ while skipping multi-GB caches. Never add -uu (drags caches in). Never conclude a file "doesn't exist" from one search — confirm with ls -la.
  • Don't trust cached mental models: before claiming "memory is current" or "journal is up to date", run wc -c memory/work-journal.md in the same turn. Numbers and the commands that produced them travel together.

See the memory skill (skills/memory/SKILL.md) for the full operating basics.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: By default every lazar -p invocation starts cold: no prior messages, just your prompt plus the system prompt. Sessions are the opt-in continuity mechanism.

docs.title: Resuming
docs.text:
lazar -p --session <id> "what did we decide about X?"
lazar -p --resume "continue"

With --session <id> or --resume, prior turns from the session log are prepended to the message array (bounded by LAZAR_SESSION_HISTORY_MAX_BYTES). This is the only mode in which referential prompts ("yes", "do that") resolve against real prior turns.

docs.title: The event stream
docs.text:
Everything — prompts, responses, tool calls, tool results — is appended as JSONL to ~/lazar/logs/stream.jsonl, one JSON object per line with fields like {kind, ts_ms, content, command, ...}. This is the "infinite memory" log: the kernel records it but does not auto-load it.

Never cat the log

stream.jsonl can be megabytes. Reading it whole will exceed the model context window and the API will reject the request. Use the bounded recipes from the load-context skill:

tail -n 200 ~/lazar/logs/stream.jsonl | tail -c 50000

jq is your friend for field extraction.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text: The kernel auto-rotates at LAZAR_LOG_MAX_BYTES (default ~10MB) and keeps LAZAR_LOG_ARCHIVE_KEEP archives. A log-rotation hook fires after each rotation. The _meta/log-rotation skill exists for richer archive summaries but is optional.

docs.title: Referential prompts without a session
docs.text: If the operator forgot --session and sends "yes" / "continue", do not infer the referent from recent tool output — that is the documented #1 source of "executes the wrong thing confidently" errors. Either load context from the log with the bounded recipe, or ask a one-line clarifying question.

docs.title: Session env
docs.text:
• LAZAR_SESSION_ID — current session id, set by the kernel.
  • LAZAR_SESSION_HISTORY_MAX_BYTES — cap on replayed history.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text: Skills are lazar's only extension mechanism. The kernel is immutable; all capability growth happens by writing folders under ~/lazar/skills/.

docs.title: Anatomy
docs.text:
A skill is a directory with a SKILL.md:

skills/
├── INDEX.md                  one line per skill: name — description
├── <name>/
│   ├── SKILL.md              frontmatter (name, description) + instructions
│   └── ...                   scripts, templates, fixtures the skill needs
└── _meta/                    skills about being lazar (subagent, memory,
                              load-context, harness, self-patch, ...)

INDEX.md is the discovery surface — the agent reads it at the start of any non-trivial task, then reads the relevant SKILL.md in full before acting.

docs.title: Writing one
docs.text:
1. mkdir ~/lazar/skills/<name>
  2. Write SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter:
---
name: my-skill
description: One sentence — when to load this skill.
---

# my-skill

Instructions, recipes, exact commands, failure modes.
  1. Append one line to skills/INDEX.md.

Keep SKILL.md concrete: exact commands with absolute paths, bounded recipes (tail -n 200, never cat an unbounded file), and the failure modes that motivated the skill.

docs.title: The _meta/ skills
docs.text:
_meta/ holds the operating basics, and they outrank other skills on conflict:

  • memory — persistence across sessions (memory/ notes, work journal).
  • verify — the [VERIFY] grounding contract.
  • subagent — delegation via bin/lazar-spawn / pack-and-spawn.sh.
  • load-context — bounded recipes for reading logs/stream.jsonl.
  • harness — durable ranked lessons (harness.py add).
  • self-patch — fix your own recurring failures; draft kernel proposals, never self-apply.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Skills live in skills/ — never patch bin/ or src/ to add behavior.
  • A skill that shells out must respect the sandbox write zones when guardrails are on (skills/, memory/, workspace/, /tmp).
  • If a capability is missing, write a skill — don't wait for a kernel change.

docs.title: Sub-agents
docs.text: Delegation goes through one locked binary: bin/lazar-spawn. Raw lazar -p from inside an agent session is vetoed by a pre-tool hook.

docs.title: Spawning
docs.text:
# Recommended: context pack + dispatch
bash "$LAZAR_HOME/skills/_meta/subagent/pack-and-spawn.sh" <task-id> \
  --objective "..." --out /absolute/deliverable --path /absolute/input

# Lower-level: you already wrote the prompt file
bash "$LAZAR_HOME/bin/lazar-spawn" <task-id> <prompt-file>

docs.title: The context pack (BRIEF.md)
docs.text:
Children are strangers with a filesystem — no parent history. Write workspace/tasks/<id>/BRIEF.md containing:

  1. Imperative objective
  2. Absolute input/output paths
  3. SUCCESS: + EXPECT-VERIFY: claims authored by the parent
  4. Relevant skill names
  5. Prior decisions / constraints (≤ ~20 lines)
  6. Out-of-scope list
  7. RESULT.md protocol (first line DONE or BLOCKED)

lazar-spawn re-checks the EXPECT-VERIFY claims against the filesystem and returns {"status":"ok","matched":true} only if they hold. Trust matched, not child prose.

docs.title: Bounds
docs.text: Bound Default Kernel stall-nudges (in-child) bounded, LAZAR_STALL_NUDGES Per-task retries (LAZAR_SPAWN_CEILING) 2 Session spawn budget (LAZAR_SPAWN_BUDGET) 10 Wall-clock kill (LAZAR_SPAWN_TIMEOUT) 300s Recursion depth (LAZAR_DEPTH vs kernel MAX_DEPTH) 5

docs.title: The auth gotcha
docs.text: Children do not inherit the provider API key by default. A child spawned without credentials fails its first API call with 401 invalid x-api-key and the spawn returns status: fail with every claim unmet. Pass LAZAR_TOOL_INHERIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=1 on the spawn when the child needs model access (which is almost always).

docs.title: When NOT to spawn
docs.text: Routine bash, exploratory one-offs, anything whose result is stdout you need to reason on — do those in-process. Spawn only for isolated, file-verifiable units of work or parallel fan-out.

docs.title: Eval harness
docs.text: lazar ships a backend-agnostic evaluation suite that scores the harness, not the model: tool honesty, VERIFY grounding, fabrication resistance, recovery, self-learning surfaces. Two agents with the same model can score very differently — that delta is harness quality.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
• Skill: skills/harness-evals/ (vendored snapshot so --reset-all works offline).
  • Upstream: /Users/jkneen/Documents/GitHub/harness-evals — canonical, agent-agnostic; make changes there.
  • Workspace runner: workspace/evals/ with run-all.sh, kernel-evals.sh, model-evals.sh, tests/, results/.

docs.title: When to run it
docs.text:
• Comparing backends/models on the same harness.
  • Proving a harness change helped or regressed.
  • CI gates before shipping kernel/skill changes.
  • Answering "is the self-learning system actually working?"

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The same task packs run against any agent via pluggable adapters (lazar, generic command, recorded fixtures). Scores target harness behaviors: whether the agent fabricates file state, whether its [VERIFY] claims match the filesystem, whether it recovers from induced failures, and whether lessons get recorded durably.

bash ~/lazar/workspace/evals/run-all.sh     # full suite
ls   ~/lazar/workspace/evals/results/       # prior runs

See skills/harness-evals/SKILL.md for adapter configuration and pack authoring.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
agent loop — the kernel's cycle of model call → tool call → tool result → model call. Lives in the kernel only, never in the TUI or any client.

BRIEF.md — the context pack handed to a sub-agent: objective, absolute paths, SUCCESS + EXPECT-VERIFY claims, constraints, RESULT.md protocol. See Sub-agents.

continual harness — the ranked, durable lesson store in memory/harness/, managed by skills/_meta/harness/harness.py. Overview is auto-injected at session start.

event stream — logs/stream.jsonl, the append-only JSONL record of every prompt, response, tool call, and result. Recorded by the kernel, loaded only via bounded recipes.

EXPECT-VERIFY — the testable claims a parent authors for a spawned task; lazar-spawn re-checks them against the filesystem before reporting matched: true.

grounding — the discipline of proving file-state claims with real commands, enforced by the kernel's [VERIFY] contract.

guardrails — the on/off switch for sandbox + trusted-zone protections, toggled by scripts/lazar-guardrails.sh (the guardrails skill).

heartbeat / tick — the lazar --tick path: a scheduled invocation that walks maintenance phases (journal, todos, memory hygiene) with zero user questions.

hooks — user-controlled bash scripts in hooks/<event>.d/ fired by the kernel at lifecycle moments. See Hooks.

kernel — the immutable bin/lazar binary + src/ source. Read-only after build; evolution happens via skills, never kernel edits.

lazar-spawn — the locked delegation binary. The only sanctioned way to run a sub-agent; raw lazar -p from inside a session is vetoed.

memory — plain-markdown persistence under memory/. See Memory.

pack-and-spawn — skills/_meta/subagent/pack-and-spawn.sh: writes a BRIEF.md context pack then dispatches via bin/lazar-spawn.

PINNED.md — memory/PINNED.md, the session-start ground truth: provider config, code ownership, behavioral rules.

RESULT.md — the sub-agent status file; first line DONE or BLOCKED.

sandbox — the sandbox-exec profile limiting writes to skills/, memory/, workspace/, /tmp, and specific session subdirs when guardrails are on. See Concepts → Sandbox.

session — opt-in continuity via --session <id> / --resume. See Sessions.

skill — a folder under skills/ with a SKILL.md; the only extension mechanism. See Skills.

stall nudge — the kernel's bounded recovery when a turn narrates unfinished intent without acting (LAZAR_STALL_NUDGES, default 2). Never fires on questions, never unbounded.

TUI — the Go terminal client in workspace/tui/ (owner-managed). Drives lazar; contains no agent loop.

VERIFY contract — the [VERIFY]...[/VERIFY] block declaring testable filesystem claims (exists=, contains=, size_at_least=, ...). The kernel checks them and rejects ungrounded completions.

work journal — memory/work-journal.md, the durable record of completed work, harvested from the event stream.

docs.title: Skills catalogue
docs.text: As of the last ground-truth sweep, ~/lazar/skills/ holds 89 entries (ls ~/lazar/skills | wc -l): 62 general skills plus 27 _meta/ operating skills. This page is a map, not a replica — run cat ~/lazar/skills/INDEX.md for the live one-line index.

docs.title: _meta/ — operating basics
docs.text:
Skills about being lazar. These outrank other skills on conflict.

Skill Purpose memory Persistence across invocations; plain-markdown notes. load-context Bounded recipes for reading logs/stream.jsonl (never cat). subagent Delegation via bin/lazar-spawn / pack-and-spawn.sh. harness Ranked durable lessons (harness.py add/load/helpful). self-patch Fix your own recurring failures; draft kernel proposals, never self-apply. create-skill Scaffold a new skill correctly. heartbeat The --tick maintenance loop. log-harvest Distill the event stream into memory/work-journal.md. log-rotation Richer archive summaries after rotation. checkpoint / session-compression Session state snapshots and compression. health-check / first-run / session-startup Environment verification and bootstrapping. distill / distill-large Session distillation. propose-kernel-patch The only path for kernel changes (operator-applied). find-capability / semantic-recall / embed-corpus Search over skills and memory. archive-search / project-context / reviews / triage / ahe / loop / no-repeat-failed-calls / prune-baks / shell-handoff / skill-corpus-audit / session-end / create-tui Assorted maintenance and workflow skills.

docs.title: Core behavioral skills
docs.text: Skill Purpose verify (VERIFY contract) Grounding: prove claims with [VERIFY] blocks. guardrails Toggle sandbox / trusted zones. hooks-system Work with the hooks lifecycle. model / model-identity / model-tier / models Model selection and identity. provider-switch / provider-router / provider-failover Backend management (MiniMax, OpenRouter, ...). invoke-flags / env-vars CLI flags and environment reference. input-images Vision via image blocks.

Note

This catalogue drifts — skills are added constantly. The authoritative list is always ls ~/lazar/skills/ and cat ~/lazar/skills/INDEX.md.
